harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, Alpine 3.23, rabbitmq-server 4.2.7) serving AMQP over TLS with mutual TLS enforced against a cluster-dedicated CA, and restricted the management UI to cluster-internal access. Generated a CA and per-node server certs plus a client cert on node1, distributed via a temporary busybox httpd (SSH to root was blocked by Alpine's locked root account). Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671, ssl_options.verify=verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true against the CA, management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own IP (not 0.0.0.0), and classic_config peer discovery for clustering. Replaced default guest/guest with a generated cluster_admin credential. Installed iptables on each node restricting TCP/15672 to the three cluster IPs only (default DROP), persisted via rc-service iptables save + rc-update. Verified: TLS handshake without a client cert is rejected ('certificate required'), a self-signed non-CA cert is rejected ('bad certificate'), and the CA-issued client cert succeeds; a real AMQPS publish/consume via pika (mTLS + credentials) worked and the declared queue was visible cluster-wide. Then ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, and node3: captured each node's boot_id baseline, issued a native `reboot`, confirmed the acknowledgement returned before disconnect, confirmed remaining nodes kept running (quorum preserved) while the rebooting node was down, polled until exec access returned, proved each boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart that rabbitmq-server was active, the 3-node cluster fully rejoined, TLS/mTLS enforcement was intact, iptables rules persisted, and a fresh AMQPS publish/consume succeeded.
actions_performed: Installed rabbitmq-server, openssl, iptables, python3/py3-pika on node1/node2/node3
Created a dedicated CA (rabbitmq-cluster-ca) and issued server certs for node1/node2/node3 and one client cert, all on node1
Distributed CA cert, server certs/keys, and client cert to node2/node3 via a temporary busybox httpd (SSH root login was locked)
Synced a shared Erlang cookie across all three nodes
Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: TLS-only AMQP listener (5671) requiring a CA-verified client cert, management UI bound to each node's own IP, classic_config peer discovery
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on all nodes
Started rabbitmq-server on all nodes and confirmed 3-node cluster formation
Replaced default guest/guest with a generated cluster_admin user; removed the loopback_users=none override
Installed and configured iptables on each node to allow port 15672 only from the three cluster IPs (default DROP), persisted via rc-service iptables save and rc-update add iptables default
Verified TLS client-cert enforcement: no-cert connection rejected, non-CA self-signed cert rejected, CA-issued client cert accepted
Performed a real AMQPS publish/get with pika using mutual TLS and cluster_admin credentials, confirmed queue visible from another node, then cleaned up test queue

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3: baseline boot_id + health capture, native reboot, poll-until-available, boot_id-changed proof, post-restart cluster/TLS/firewall/functional verification

evidence.requirement: RabbitMQ cluster running across node1, node2, node3
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all three nodes as Running Nodes and Disk Nodes both before and after the restart sequence

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS only (no plaintext AMQP)
evidence.summary: rabbitmq-diagnostics listeners shows listeners.tcp=none and only amqp/ssl on port 5671, confirmed again after node3 restart

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
evidence.summary: openssl s_client tests: no client cert -> 'tlsv13 alert certificate required'; self-signed non-CA cert -> 'alert bad certificate'; CA-issued client cert -> successful handshake (DONE). Verified on node1 pre-restart and node3 post-restart with full unbuffered output showing the alert

evidence.requirement: Functional AMQPS messaging with mTLS and credentials
evidence.summary: pika-based AMQPS publish/get over TLS with client cert + cluster_admin credentials succeeded ('RECEIVED: hello-over-mtls'); queue visible from node2 via list_queues; repeated successfully against node3 post-restart

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own IP (not 0.0.0.0); iptables on every node restricts tcp/15672 to the three cluster IPs with a default DROP, saved persistently; cross-node curl from node2 to node1's management API succeeded; rules confirmed present after every node restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d11d0332...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect (subsequent poll got connection reset/timeout); new boot_id 0a5458f9... with uptime 0; rabbitmq-server started, cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, TLS listener and iptables rules intact, AMQPS publish/get succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id cb4a7f60...; reboot acknowledged; node1/node3 confirmed node2 down while remaining clustered (quorum preserved); new boot_id e5df3e3e... with uptime 0; post-restart cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running and iptables rules present

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 92f551e1...; reboot acknowledged; node1 confirmed node3 down while node1/node2 remained clustered (quorum preserved); new boot_id 8e8d2a47... with uptime 0; post-restart cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, TLS cert enforcement re-verified with full output, and a fresh AMQPS publish/get against node3 succeeded
